clear.agents: No instructions or tools for coding agents.

advice.installScripts: Read what these commands do before you go ahead. Rayfin apps don’t need commands of their own to install.
advice.packageSources: Make sure you know who publishes these packages, and why they don’t come from npm.
advice.packageAliases: Check that each one is the package it stands in for.
advice.packageHosts: A company’s own package registry is fine. Otherwise, find out why it doesn’t use npm’s.
advice.npmSettings: Don’t go ahead unless you know why it does this. Projects don’t need these settings.
advice.gitSettings: Don’t go ahead unless you know why they’re there. A project shared with you doesn’t need them.
advice.unreadableSettings: Don’t go ahead unless you can see what they set: npm or git may still run programs they name.
advice.gitDir: Don’t go ahead unless you know why it’s there. A project shared with you doesn’t need it.
advice.unreadableManifest: Don’t go ahead unless you can see what’s in them: npm may still run scripts or download packages from them.
advice.gitHooks: Read what the hooks run before you go ahead.
advice.editorTasks: Check what the task runs before you open the project in VS Code.
advice.mcpServers: Check what these programs are before you let a coding agent start them.
advice.programs: Find out what they’re for before you go ahead.
advice.aimedAtAi: Don’t rely on an AI’s review of this package, this one included. Read the code yourself or ask who sent it.
advice.hiddenCode: An app’s own code has no reason to hide what it does. Ask who sent it what this is.

installScripts.title: Runs commands when its packages install
installScripts.detail: npm runs {{list}} when Fabricator installs its packages, before the app opens.

packageSources.title: Gets packages from outside npm
packageSources.detail: {{list}}. npm doesn’t check code that comes from git, a website or a folder, and it can change at any time.

packageAliases.title: Installs packages under other names
packageAliases.detail: {{list}}: npm installs one package under another’s name.

npmSettings.title: Changes the programs npm runs
npmSettings.detail: {{list}}. npm would use them while it installs packages and runs scripts.

gitSettings.title: Has git settings that run programs
gitSettings.detailProject: Its git settings set {{list}}. Git runs them when it works in the folder, which Fabricator does each time it saves a version.
gitSettings.detailApp: Its git settings set {{list}}. Git runs them when it works in the folder.

unreadableSettings.title: Has settings Fabricator can’t read
unreadableSettings.detail_one: Fabricator can’t read {{list}}: it’s too large or not plain text, so it can’t tell what npm or git would run from it.
unreadableSettings.detail_other: Fabricator can’t read {{list}}: they’re too large or not plain text, so it can’t tell what npm or git would run from them.

gitDir.title: Points git at another folder
gitDir.detail: {{list}}. Git takes its settings and hooks from there, and they can run programs whenever git works in the folder.

unreadableManifest.title_one: Has an npm file Fabricator can’t read
unreadableManifest.title_other: Has npm files Fabricator can’t read
unreadableManifest.detail_one: Fabricator can’t read {{list}}: it’s too large or not plain JSON, so it can’t tell what npm would run or download from it.
unreadableManifest.detail_other: Fabricator can’t read {{list}}: they’re too large or not plain JSON, so it can’t tell what npm would run or download from them.

gitHooks.title: Sets up git hooks
gitHooks.detail: Once its packages are installed, git runs {{list}} each time a version is saved, and Fabricator saves one after each chat turn.

editorTasks.title: Runs a task when the folder opens in VS Code
editorTasks.detail: {{file}} starts a task as soon as the folder opens in VS Code, once you allow it.

mcpServers.title: Adds MCP servers for coding agents
mcpServers.detail: {{file}} starts {{list}} for coding agents that use it.

programs.title: Includes programs
programs.detail: It holds {{list}}. Rayfin apps don’t need programs of their own, and Copilot can’t read them.

aimedAtAi.title: Has text aimed at AI tools
aimedAtAi.detail: {{list}}. Text that tries to steer AI reviewers or coding agents is a warning sign.

hiddenCode.title: Has hidden or encoded code
hiddenCode.detail: {{list}}: code written so people can’t read it.
